title: Coronavirus outbreak: Nova Scotia expects to hit COVID-19 peak in late April, early May | FULL
description: Nova Scotia Premier Stephen McNeil and the province's chief medical officer of health, Dr. Robert Strang, held a briefing Wednesday afternoon updating the latest COVID-19 numbers and detailing the province's efforts to curb the spread of the virus.  Strang reported 32 new cases of COVID-19 in the province, bringing the total number of cases to 549. Nine individuals were in hospital as of April 15, and 137 had recovered.  Strang also said that Nova Scotia can “likely expect” to hit its COVID-19 peak in either late April or early May based on the number of cases in other provinces, as well as their trajectory of cases. He said this could mean that they would not be able to ease restrictive measures until June.  He noted that those measures, too, will not be relaxed all at once, saying, “We have to take them off carefully and gradually, monitoring the disease epidemiology and being prepared to course-correct if necessary.”  Over 17,000 Nova Scotia residents have been tested for COVID-19 with negative results. Nova Scotia Premier Stephen McNeil and the province's chief medical officer of health, Dr. Robert Strang, held a briefing Wednesday afternoon updating the latest COVID-19 numbers and detailing the province's efforts to curb the spread of the virus. Strang reported 32 new cases of COVID-19 in the province, bringing the total number of cases to 549. Nine individuals were in hospital as of April 15, and 137 had recovered. Strang also said that Nova Scotia can “likely expect” to hit its COVID-19 peak in either late April or early May based on the number of cases in other provinces, as well as their trajectory of cases. He said this could mean that they would not be able to ease restrictive measures until June. He noted that those measures, too, will not be relaxed all at once, saying, “We have to take them off carefully and gradually, monitoring the disease epidemiology and being prepared to course-correct if necessary.” Over 17,000 Nova Scotia residents have been tested for COVID-19 with negative results. Strang reported 32 new cases of COVID-19 in the province, bringing the total number of cases to 549. Nine individuals were in hospital as of April 15, and 137 had recovered. Strang also said that Nova Scotia can “likely expect” to hit its COVID-19 peak in either late April or early May based on the number of cases in other provinces, as well as their trajectory of cases.
